definitions.gloss: to be in want of; to lack; to go without
definitions.explanation: To experience a shortage or lack of something necessary. Often used in the negative ({不自由|ふじゆう}しない) to mean having plenty.

examples.japanese: {食|た}べ{物|もの}に{不自由|ふじゆう}する。
お{金|かね}に{不自由|ふじゆう}しない{生活|せいかつ}をしている。
examples.english: I live a life where I don't lack for money.

examples.japanese: {海外|かいがい}では{言葉|ことば}に{不自由|ふじゆう}して{困|こま}ることがある。
examples.english: Overseas, I sometimes have trouble because of the language barrier.

notes:
{不自由|ふじゆう}する means to be in want of or to lack something necessary. The pattern is 〜に{不自由|ふじゆう}する.

KEY POINT:
Very frequently used in the negative: 〜に{不自由|ふじゆう}しない means "to have no shortage of" or "to want for nothing."

COMMON PATTERNS:
- お{金|かね}に{不自由|ふじゆう}しない (to want for nothing financially)
- {食|た}べ{物|もの}に{不自由|ふじゆう}する (to be short of food)
- {言葉|ことば}に{不自由|ふじゆう}する (to struggle with the language)
- {生活|せいかつ}に{不自由|ふじゆう}する (to have an inconvenient life)

RELATED:
The noun {不自由|ふじゆう} alone means inconvenience or disability ({不自由|ふじゆう}な{生活|せいかつ} = an inconvenient life; {体|からだ}が{不自由|ふじゆう} = physically disabled).

OPPOSITE:
{自由|じゆう} (freedom, free).
